children: OTTAWA--Retail sales in Canada fell for the first month this year in July, with weakness at general-merchandise retailers in the country leading broad declines.
Sales fell 0.7% from the previous month to a seasonally adjusted 73.7 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.25 billion, Statistics Canada said Thursday.
The drop in sales, the first since December, was roughly in line with the data agency's preliminary estimate sales fell 0.8% for the month.
Compared with a year earlier, retail sales in July were up 5.1%.
The agency said an early tally of receipts indicate sales increased 1.3% in August, though the figure was based on responses from 57.8% of the retailers surveyed and will be revised.
